one_liner: Educational ~300-line CUDA C++ FlashAttention-2 forward kernel; 4-6% faster than flash-attn on one RTX 5090 shape, 3% slower than cuDNN.
what_it_does: 07_attention in this learning repository holds five progressively optimized FlashAttention-2-style forward kernels (attention_v1.cu to attention_v5.cu), exposed to Python through a PyTorch C++ extension as sdpa_v1 to sdpa_v5(Q, K, V). Inputs are contiguous bf16 tensors [batch, heads, seq, 128]; the output is a new tensor of the same shape. There is no backward pass, causal mask, attention mask, dropout, variable-length or GQA support; it is a worked example to read, not a library to depend on.
how_it_is_fast: FlashAttention-2 partitioning: each 128-thread block owns a 64-row query tile, the four warps split those rows, and every warp streams through 64-row K/V tiles with an online softmax (running row max and sum, rescaling the output accumulator) so the attention matrix is never materialized. Data moves global to shared with cp.async into XOR-swizzled shared memory to avoid bank conflicts, then to registers with ldmatrix.x4 (transposed for V), and both matmuls use bf16 mma.sync.m16n8k16 tensor-core instructions with fp32 accumulators. v5 double-buffers K and overlaps the next K and V loads with the softmax and the matmuls (2-stage cp.async pipeline).
when_to_use: You want a short, readable reference for a near-roofline FlashAttention-2 forward pass in raw CUDA C++ and inline PTX, with each optimization isolated in its own file (swizzling, pipelining, ldmatrix.x4).

You are writing your own attention kernel for consumer Blackwell (RTX 5090, sm_120) or Ampere/Ada-class GPUs and need a working baseline to modify, for example to try MXFP8/NVFP4 MMA, which the author cites as the reason for using CUDA C++ instead of Triton.
Non-causal bf16 prefill-style attention with head_dim 128 and sequence lengths that are multiples of 64, where you can verify the result yourself against F.scaled_dot_product_attention.
when_not_to_use: Production inference or training: use PyTorch SDPA with the cuDNN backend (203.61 vs 197.74 TFLOPS on the author's own benchmark), flash-attn or FlashInfer, which handle masks, varlen, GQA and backward.
Any head_dim other than 128: the host wrapper prints an error and calls exit(1), terminating the Python process.
Sequence lengths not divisible by 64: the kernel has no tail handling or KV masking, so partial tiles read out of bounds and produce wrong results.
Causal attention, masks, dropout, fp16 or fp8 inputs, or training (no backward kernel).
Anything you need to redistribute: the repository has no license file.

integration.form: source-drop (PyTorch C++/CUDA extension JIT-built with torch.utils.cpp_extension.load)
integration.dependencies: PyTorch with CUDA (cpp_extension, pybind11), CUDA toolkit (README results with CUDA 12.9); the harness also uses triton.testing.do_bench and pandas, and flash-attn optionally
integration.min_toolchain: CUDA 12.x with an sm_80+ target (mma.sync bf16, cp.async, ldmatrix); README results use CUDA 12.9; exact minimum not documented
integration.platforms: NVIDIA GPUs sm_80 and newer that support mma.sync bf16 (measured only on RTX 5090, sm_120); not for AMD/Intel
integration.thread_safety: not documented; kernels launch on the default CUDA stream rather than PyTorch's current stream
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same (Q, K, V) to O semantics as F.scaled_dot_product_attention for non-causal, unmasked, bf16, head_dim 128, contiguous [B, H, L, D] inputs only

gotchas: attention.cpp does not check dtype, device or contiguity and takes raw data pointers, flattening batch x heads; a transposed or non-contiguous tensor gives silently wrong output.
Kernels launch with <<<>>> on the default stream, ignoring torch.cuda.current_stream(); code running on other streams can race or serialize.
Softmax uses the fast-math __expf and P is rounded to bf16 before the P@V matmul (as in FA2); the harness checks output only with torch.testing.assert_close defaults on one random shape.
The harness default is --bs 4 while the README table states bs=1; reproduce with --bs 1 to compare numbers.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick this over FlashAttention-3, ThunderKittens or SageAttention only when you want to learn from or fork a minimal kernel: FA3 targets Hopper, SageAttention trades precision for speed on RTX 5090-class GPUs, and both are maintained libraries, whereas this is roughly 300 lines you can read in one sitting.
verified_claims_summary: On one RTX 5090 capped at 400W (CUDA 12.9, bf16, head_dim 128, 8 heads, 4096 queries x 8192 keys, non-causal), the author's harness timed v5 at 197.74 TFLOPS (median from triton do_bench), against 190.58 for the flash-attn package (about 1.04x) and 186.73 for PyTorch SDPA's FlashAttention backend (about 1.06x), but behind SDPA's cuDNN backend at 203.61 TFLOPS (about 0.97x). PyTorch and flash-attn versions and the host CPU are not stated.
